questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'The cat chased the mouse.'

options.option_text: The mouse was chased by the cat.
The mouse has been chased by the cat.
The mouse is being chased by the cat.
The mouse chased the cat.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Simple past active → simple past passive: 'was + past participle'. The object 'mouse' becomes the subject.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'She is singing a song.'

options.option_text: A song was being sung by her.
A song is being sung by her.
A song has been sung by her.
A song is sung by her.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Present continuous active → 'is/am/are + being + past participle': 'is being sung by her'.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'They have completed the project.'

options.option_text: The project was completed by them.
The project has been completed by them.
The project is completed by them.
The project had been completed by them.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Present perfect active → 'has/have + been + past participle': 'has been completed by them'.

questions.stem: Change to active voice: 'The letter was written by Ram.'

options.option_text: Ram writes the letter.
Ram wrote the letter.
Ram is writing the letter.
Ram has written the letter.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Past passive ('was written') → past simple active: 'Ram wrote the letter'.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'Will you help me?'

options.option_text: Will I be helped by you?
Am I helped by you?
Can I be helped by you?
Would I be helped by you?

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Will + object + be + past participle': 'Will I be helped by you?' The interrogative structure and tense (will) are preserved.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'Open the door.' (imperative)

options.option_text: The door is opened.
Let the door be opened.
The door must be opened.
The door should be opened.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Imperative passive = 'Let + object + be + past participle': 'Let the door be opened'.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'She will complete the task tomorrow.'

options.option_text: The task will be completed by her tomorrow.
The task was completed by her tomorrow.
The task is completed by her tomorrow.
The task has been completed by her tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A is correct. Future simple passive = 'will + be + past participle': 'The task will be completed by her tomorrow'.

questions.stem: Change to active voice: 'The cake was eaten by the children.'

options.option_text: The children ate the cake.
The children eat the cake.
The children will eat the cake.
The children have eaten the cake.

questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Was eaten' (past passive) → 'ate' (past simple active): 'The children ate the cake'.

questions.stem: Change to passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my wallet.' (agent is unknown)

options.option_text: My wallet was stolen by someone.
My wallet has been stolen.
My wallet is stolen.
My wallet had been stolen.

questions.explanation: B is correct. When the agent is vague ('someone'), it is omitted in the passive. Present perfect → 'has been stolen'. Option A keeps 'someone' which is unusual to specify.

questions.stem: Which options correctly express the passive of: 'People believe that he is honest'?

options.option_text: It is believed that he is honest.
He is believed to be honest.
Both options A and B are correct passive forms.
Neither option is a valid passive form.

questions.explanation: C is correct. Two valid passive constructions exist for 'people believe that S V': (1) 'It is believed that he is honest' (preparatory-it construction) and (2) 'He is believed to be honest' (raising construction). Both are standard.
